Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
707 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A cold front will bring a chance for a few showers and
  thunderstorms Saturday afternoon/evening through very early
  Sunday. 
 
- Next week's outlook features seasonably hot and humid conditions
  with isolated afternoon showers and storms possible.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 212 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Summer persists in Southeast Texas as hot and humid conditions
continue thanks to high pressure and abundant sunshine.
Temperatures this afternoon have rising into the mid 90s for much
of the region with heat indices in the 100-105 degree range.
Another warm and muggy night is expected tonight, but then on
Saturday I have something to discuss that isn't just high pressure
and heat. An upper-level disturbance moving through the Midwest
will push a weak "cold" front into Southeast Texas tomorrow into
tomorrow night. Because the front is so weak, exact FROPA timing
is still uncertain - but it will likely be in the late afternoon
into the evening hours from north to south. Isolated showers will
begin to pop up across the Piney Woods region as early as the 
morning hours as the front approaches from the north. By the
afternoon and into the evening hours, isolated to scattered
showers and thunderstorms will begin to pop-up down along the I-10
corridor and the coast. Severe thunderstorms are not expected, but
gusty winds and a localized downpour will always be possible with
any thunderstorms that develop. 

High temperatures on Saturday will likely be limited by increasing
cloud coverage and any showers or thunderstorms that develop. But,
we will likely still see temperatures rising into the mid to upper
90s across the region with heat indices in the triple digits. 
Have opted out of issuing any Heat Advisories for tomorrow due to 
the uncertainty of the FROPA timing - but, there is a possibility 
that areas along and south of I-10 will approach Heat Advisory 
thresholds if the FROPA is later than expected. 

This "cold" front will really not bring in any cooler weather - in
fact temperatures may even be a degree to two hotter on Sunday
than tomorrow. This is because while cooler air won't be filtering
in, drier air will be allowing for warmer ambient temperatures.
Hot weather will continue through the remainder of the week with
Monday likely being the hottest day of the week with high
temperatures nearing 100 degrees.

Fowler

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 657 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

A weak cold front will attempt to move through the terminals Saturday
afternoon, bringing rain and storm chances for most terminals. A 
few -SHRA are possible near KCLL and KUTS around 11Z- 13Z, with 
the best chances (20 - 35%) in the afternoon. Confidence in 
SHRA/TSRA for terminals from IAH coastward is low; therefore, have
only included PROB30 from mid afternoon through early evening for
this forecast package. Light to occasionally moderate WSW winds 
will prevail Saturday. Overall, expect SCT to BKN mid to high 
clouds, with FEW/SCT low clouds possible early Saturday. Outside 
of any TSRA, VFR conditions can be expected through the period.

JM

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 212 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

South to southwesterly winds around 10-15kt will persist through
Saturday morning with low seas. An approaching front will lead to
a strengthening of the winds Saturday afternoon into Saturday 
night to around 15-20kt, so small craft will likely need to 
exercise caution. Seas will increase to around 2-4ft Saturday
night into Sunday morning following the increasing winds. An
isolated shower or thunderstorm will be possible Saturday evening
into Saturday night as the front approaches the coastal waters,
but chances are pretty low (below 20%). A more west-southwesterly
wind will be possible on Sunday following the front. 

Light to occasionally moderate onshore flow will persist through 
next week with low seas. 

Fowler 

&&

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
632 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat continues through Saturday with afternoon highs in 
the mid to upper 90s and maximum heat indices of 102-109F.

- A weak frontal boundary will move through the region Saturday
  night into Sunday bringing a 30-60% chance of rain. Some 
  slightly drier air may work into the region Sunday, but both 
  high and low temperatures will remain largely unchanged. 

- A few, diurnally driven, afternoon thunderstorms are expected to
  develop each day next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Thursday)
Issued at 1213 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Friday afternoon surface analysis shows weak high pressure over the 
northern Gulf while a frontal system is in the Plains. Aloft, 
ridging extends from the Pacific coast to the Southern Plains, while 
a shortwave trough is moving into the Great Lakes region. Ridging 
aloft will bring about another hot and dry afternoon today, with 
highs reaching into the mid to upper 90s. A few spots, particularly 
along the coast, may touch heat advisory criteria briefly this 
afternoon, but overall heat indices should top out in the mid-100s.

Moving into the weekend, upper level ridging begins to retrograde 
westward tonight into tomorrow, while the aforementioned shortwave 
trough dives southeast across the Midwest and evolves into a broader 
scale trough over the E CONUS by early Sunday. The evolution of this 
upper trough will give a surface front/low pressure system a push 
south across the Plains and into the lower MS Valley over the 
weekend. This boundary is expected to make its way into the Ark-La-
Tex tomorrow afternoon and to the coast by Sunday morning. While 
this will mean very little for us temperature wise, with highs still 
reaching into the mid-90s both Sat and Sun, it will bring a bit of 
slightly drier air with a brief north/northwest wind shift along 
with a small chance for showers and storms late Sat into Sun. 

Any repreive from the dog days of summer that this front is able 
to bring will be short lived, with SW/S surface winds returning on
Monday as the front becomes increasingly washed out overhead 
through early next week. At the same time, upper level troughing 
will begin to weaken and retreat northward, losing its hold over 
the E CONUS by late Monday. In its wake, broad flat ridging will 
again build across the southern CONUS. With somewhat weak ridging 
overhead, a few afternoon diurnally driven showers and storms will
be possible each day next week, but coverage will be fairly
isolated to widely scattered at best. With little day to day 
change in the synoptic pattern next week, afternoon highs will 
generally range from the mid to upper 90s each day with overnight 
lows in the mid to upper 70s. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 627 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

VFR conditions will prevail through the taf period with light
south southwesterly winds prevailing tonight. A weak frontal
boundary will approach the region Saturday with it's gradient
increasing southwesterly winds to around 10 knots with gusts up to
20. VFR cloud cover will increase during the afternoon. There will
be a 20% chance of a small shower or thunderstorm through the
afternoon. The frontal boundary is not expected to move through
until beyond this forecast period so no appreciable wind shift is
expected.

Jones

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1213 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Light southwesterly winds and low seas will continue through 
tonight. A weak boundary will approach from the north tomorrow, 
before moving through the coastal waters early Sunday. As this 
boundary approaches it will tighten the pressure gradient slightly, 
allowing winds to increase to around 15kts with gusts to around 
20kts throughout tomorrow. By Sat night into Sun winds increase a 
bit further with sustained 15-20kts and gusts to 20-25kts. The 
boundary will also increase thunderstorm chances late Sat through 
Sun. An exercise caution statement has been issued for tomorrow, and 
a SCA may briefly be needed Sat night/Sun morning. Light southerly 
flow becomes reestablished Monday through the rest of the week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1213 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Hot and humid conditions will continue through Saturday. Rain 
chances will increase Saturday night into Sunday as an upper level 
trough and weak frontal boundary approach the area. A brief period 
of northwesterly winds are expected Sunday bringing some slightly 
drier air into the region. Minimum RH's Sunday afternoon are 
expected to be in the 35-50% range. Winds will turn back out of the 
south Sunday night into Monday. Isolated afternoon thunderstorms 
will develop each day next week.

&&
